title: Cross-SDK incremental fetching, retry/backoff, and streaming schema evolution spec
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
PRD / scope: Define a single, testable set of behavioral requirements and acceptance criteria for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs implementing incremental fetching (cursor-based pagination), robust retry/backoff semantics, and forward-compatible streaming event schemas. Goal is to avoid per-language divergence that caused three previous rollback patches and to make client behavior predictable for production workloads.

Key scope items (in-scope):
- Cursor-based pagination contract (opaque cursor, has_more, item_count hints, server-provided page_size limits).
- Retry semantics for idempotent and non-idempotent endpoints; idempotency key guidance and default backoff/jitter policy.
- Streaming APIs: canonical envelope schema, resume tokens for reconnects, and guidance for SSE/WebSocket/gRPC transports.
- Compatibility rules for adding fields or event types in streaming (schema_version, optional fields, and deprecation windows).
- Language-specific wrapper ergonomics only where necessary (iterator/async iterator patterns).

Out of scope: SDK-specific UI helper components, platform-side server implementation work (except where API surface must be changed), non-HTTP experimental transports.

Motivation / problem statements:
1) Teams observed inconsistent pagination semantics between Python and TS SDKs leading to off-by-one bugs in shardable ingestion jobs.
2) Retry behaviors differed (linear vs exponential, jitter missing), causing cascading duplicate requests to downstream partners.
3) Streaming clients broke when server added optional meta fields because SDK deserializers were strict.

High-level decisions (so far):
- Use opaque, base64-url cursor tokens from server; clients must treat tokens as black boxes. Do not expose internals in SDK helpers.
- Default retry policy: exponential backoff with full jitter, base 100ms, cap 5s, max attempts 5 for idempotent GET-like operations. Non-idempotent operations default to no automatic retry; provide an explicit opt-in with idempotency_key header.
- Streaming envelope: all stream messages must include top-level string field "schema_version" and "event_type". Fields added in minor schema versions must be optional. SDKs must ignore unknown fields by default and expose the raw payload for advanced usage.
- Resume tokens: server will emit a resume_token field in stream checkpoints; SDKs must offer a resume() API that takes the last resume_token and replays from the server where supported.

Acceptance criteria (see separate list for tests and docs):
- All three SDKs implement cursor-based pagination with identical semantics (cursor handling, next_cursor naming, has_more boolean).
- Retry behavior is unit-tested to conform to the default parameters and allows overrides via config objects.
- Streaming clients can reconnect using resume_token and replay at least the last acknowledged event.
- SDKs tolerate additional fields in stream events without throwing or breaking iteration.
- Language idiomatic APIs: Python async iterator, TS AsyncIterable, Go channel/iterator pattern.

Deliverables:
- Updated SDK spec doc, test matrix, language-specific examples, migration guide, and canary rollout plan.

Non-functional requirements:
- Minimal performance overhead: pagination helpers should not introduce more than ~2% additional latency in hot paths.
- Backwards compatibility: follow semver for SDKs; changes that affect existing call signatures require a major bump and documented migration path.

Notes on trade-offs:
- We choose opaque cursors (server-driven) over offset because it enables robust hot-reload and compaction on server but makes debugging harder; provide a server-side debug endpoint for internal use.
- Defaulting to no retry for non-idempotent ops reduces risk of duplicates for customers but increases client burden; we provide an easy opt-in pattern with idempotency keys.
acceptance_criteria: Each SDK exposes a Pagination.PagedIterator (or idiomatic equivalent) that yields items and exposes a next_cursor string and has_more boolean.

Default retry policy implemented: exponential backoff with full jitter; base=100ms, cap=5000ms, max_attempts=5 for idempotent endpoints. Configurable via client.retry = { base, cap, max_attempts, multiplier }.
Non-idempotent endpoints do not retry by default; SDK exposes client.callWithIdempotency(payload, idempotencyKey) to enable safe retries.
Streaming envelope respected: every stream message parsed without errors when unknown keys are present; SDK exposes raw_event.json to callers.
Resume semantics: SDK can reconnect with resume_token and continue emitting events with no duplicates beyond the last checkpoint; unit+integration test coverage included.
Language ergonomics verified: Python AsyncIterator, TS AsyncIterable & Node EventEmitter fallback, Go channel-based iteration with context cancellation.
Backward/forward compatibility test: When server emits an added optional field, older SDK versions continue to function without exceptions for at least 90% of recorded integration scenarios.
Documentation and migration guide published: code samples for migrating from offset-based pagination (if used) to cursor-based and guidance for handling resume_token edge cases.
Canary rollout executed: 10% traffic for 48 hours; rollback plan and monitoring dashboards in console (latency, error-rate, duplicate-detection) in place.
Automated test matrix: end-to-end tests for Python/TS/Go that validate pagination, retries under transient failures (HTTP 502/503), and streaming reconnection behavior.
